sets.name: PCI / SOC 2 evidence
sets.description: The auditor's questions, not the engineer's: is this a control gap, is it in scope, and how long has the clock been running. Six answers in one request.

audit_disposition.instructions: Decide how this finding would be presented to an auditor, based on whether a control is working, missing, or out of scope.

criteria.evidence-ok: A functioning control already covers this: internal-only asset, low exploitability, normal patch cadence applies. Attach the evidence and move on.
criteria.exception-request: The control cannot be met as written but risk is bounded; raise a time-boxed exception with the compensating control named.
criteria.control-gap: A control that should exist is missing on an in-scope system: internet-exposed, payments or PII classification, or actively exploited.
criteria.out-of-scope: The asset does not belong in the audit boundary at all; record the exclusion rationale.

control_gap_severity.instructions: Grade the size of the control gap for this finding, independent of who owns fixing it.

criteria.name: cosmetic
criteria.description: Documentation or naming issue; no control is actually absent.

criteria.name: minor
criteria.description: A control is late or partially applied on a low-value internal asset.

criteria.name: major
criteria.description: A required control is absent on an in-scope system, but exposure is limited.

criteria.name: reportable
criteria.description: A required control is absent on an internet-exposed in-scope system, or the flaw is already being exploited.

cardholder_data_in_scope.instructions: Answer yes if this asset's data classification puts it inside the cardholder data environment: payments data is in scope, internal or corporate data generally is not.

needs_compensating_control.instructions: Answer yes if remediation cannot be completed before the audit and a compensating control must be documented instead: exposure plus a missing control is the pattern.

finding_age_pressure.instructions: Estimate how much of the remediation window has already been consumed. Known-exploited or widely exploited flaws have effectively no remaining grace period; quiet internal findings have plenty.

criteria.name: under-7-days
criteria.description: Fresh finding on a low-risk asset; the standard window is intact.

criteria.name: 7-to-30-days
criteria.description: Normal SLA territory: schedule it inside the current cycle.

criteria.name: 31-to-90-days
criteria.description: The window has slipped; expect an exception or an escalation.

criteria.name: over-90-days
criteria.description: Long past due, or the flaw is actively exploited so the clock is irrelevant.

scope_ambiguous.instructions: Answer yes when the state does not make the audit boundary decidable: the asset name, tier or data classification is too thin to say whether it is in scope.

sets.name: Regulatory notification
sets.description: A narrower set for legal handoff: would this trigger a notification duty, and who has to hear about it first.

notification_likelihood.instructions: How likely is it that an incident on this asset creates a notification duty under GDPR, state breach laws or contractual obligations?

criteria.name: unlikely
criteria.description: No personal or payment data and no business-critical role; nothing to notify.

criteria.name: possible
criteria.description: Corporate data or a tier-2 role; a duty depends on facts not in the state.

criteria.name: likely
criteria.description: Payments or PII classification, or an exposed system where personal data is plausible.

criteria.name: imminent
criteria.description: Actively exploited, internet-exposed, and holding regulated data.

notification_path.instructions: Choose the first communication step, not the legal conclusion.

criteria.no-action: No notification duty is plausible from the state; record the decision and close.
criteria.log-internally: Track it in the risk register; no external party needs to know yet.
criteria.counsel-review: The duty is arguable and the facts are thin: route to counsel before committing to anything.
criteria.notify-regulator: The duty is clear from exposure plus regulated data; start the clock and notify.

personal_data_impact.instructions: Answer yes if a breach of this asset would plausibly affect identified individuals, judged from data classification and the asset's role.
